import ctypes
import numpy as np

# Load the required libraries in the correct order
ctypes.CDLL("/usr/local/gsl/lib/libgslcblas.so", mode=ctypes.RTLD_GLOBAL)
gsl = ctypes.CDLL("/usr/local/gsl/lib/libgsl.so")

# Define the function prototype for gsl_stats_min
# double gsl_stats_min(const double data[], size_t stride, size_t n);
gsl.gsl_stats_min.argtypes = [ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_double), ctypes.c_size_t, ctypes.c_size_t]
gsl.gsl_stats_min.restype = ctypes.c_double

def find_minimum(data):
    """Find the minimum value in a list of double-precision floating-point numbers using GSL."""
    # Convert the input list to a numpy array of type double
    np_data = np.array(data, dtype=np.float64)
    # Get a pointer to the array data
    data_ptr = np_data.ctypes.data_as(ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_double))
    # Call the GSL function
    result = gsl.gsl_stats_min(data_ptr, 1, len(data))
    return result

def assert_test():
    """Run assertion-based test cases to validate correctness."""
    # Test case 1: Simple array
    data = [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, -1.0, 5.0]
    assert find_minimum(data) == -1.0, "Test case 1 failed"

    # Test case 2: Array with all positive values
    data = [10.5, 20.3, 5.1, 15.2]
    assert find_minimum(data) == 5.1, "Test case 2 failed"

    # Test case 3: Array with all negative values
    data = [-10.5, -20.3, -5.1, -15.2]
    assert find_minimum(data) == -20.3, "Test case 3 failed"

    # Test case 4: Array with a single element
    data = [42.0]
    assert find_minimum(data) == 42.0, "Test case 4 failed"

    # Test case 5: Array with repeated minimum values
    data = [3.0, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0]
    assert find_minimum(data) == 1.0, "Test case 5 failed"

    print("All test cases passed!")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    assert_test()
